title: Malignant hyperthermia
story: A fit 35-year-old man on the table, breathing room air: premedicated with midazolam and fentanyl, preoxygenated, induced with propofol and succinylcholine, intubated and maintained on sevoflurane 2 %. The jaw is stiff after the succinylcholine. Minutes into surgery the EtCO₂ climbs at the same ventilation and the heart rate rises. His phenotype is the TYPICAL one (the calcium leak takes the whole-body VO₂ to × 2.5); untreated, the EtCO₂ passes 100 mmHg, the pH falls to 7.0, the muscle is injured by the ATP it cannot pay for and the potassium it releases arrests him in VF about 119 minutes after the succinylcholine, at 38.8 °C with K⁺ 9.4 — hyperkalaemia, not the temperature, is what kills. A fulminant phenotype (× 5) arrests at about 27 minutes. Run the MH crisis: trigger off, oxygen, hyperventilation, dantrolene, cooling and the potassium.

objectives.text: Name malignant hyperthermia from the monitor: EtCO₂ above 45 mmHg at the same ventilation, tachycardia (instructor-assessed)
Call the MH crisis (stop sevoflurane, O₂ 100 % at 10 L/min, hyperventilate) within 120 s of the early signs (EtCO₂ above 45 mmHg at the same ventilation)
Give dantrolene 2.5 mg/kg within 300 s of calling the crisis

objectives: Repeat dantrolene 2.5 mg/kg within 600 s of the first dose while EtCO₂ is still above 45 mmHg

objectives.text: Treat the potassium (calcium chloride, insulin with dextrose) within 300 s of K⁺ rising above 5.5 mmol/L
Hyperventilation kept until EtCO₂ has stayed below 40 mmHg for 2 min, then ventilation normalised (back to 12 × 500)

takeHome: A rising EtCO₂ at the same ventilation with a rising heart rate: think of MH early.
Trigger off, 100 % oxygen at high flow, hyperventilation, and dantrolene 2.5 mg/kg.
Keep hyperventilating until the EtCO₂ has stayed down, and treat the potassium.
notes: Showcase case (Stage 11; the induction sequence E119, 2026-10-24). MODELED: the physiology produces every change; the buttons only give what their label says. Oxygen is never implicit (E121): he breathes room air until Preoxygenate (face mask, 100 %), and the ventilator FiO₂ 0.5 comes with Intubate; induce without Preoxygenate and the apnoea before the tube desaturates. The MH condition starts at the succinylcholine (Induce); on this sequence the early signs come about 3.9 min after it (the premedication has left the CO₂ up). E134: the phenotype on the condition event is the severity input — `typical` here, `fulminant` for the × 5 course. Measured course and bands: docs/plans/stage-11-scenarios.md; this sequence: the E119 rows of docs/showcase/SHOWCASE-2-RUN-SHEET.md.
